entries.title: Way of the Samurai

emulation.emulator: PCSX2; PPSSPP for the PSP port
emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 with an owned PS2 copy for the primary route. PPSSPP is only for the Japan-only PSP version.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PS2 assets and presentation with emulator-side resolution and filtering improvements.

primary.why: The Western PS2 release is complete, localized, and based on the improved feature set later reflected by Japan's Kanzenban release; PCSX2 gives it the best practical fidelity route from an owned copy.
primary.how_to_play: Play an owned PS2 copy on original hardware or use PCSX2 with an owned copy for cleaner capture. Use the Japanese PSP version only if you specifically want the portable release.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PS2 release; PCSX2 can improve capture resolution from an owned copy.
all_releases.reason: primary: complete localized release and best practical fidelity route through PS2 emulation.

all_releases.fidelity: Japan-only Kanzenban budget/update release on PS2.
all_releases.reason: skip: useful historical update, but not the English primary route and no sourced advantage over the Western PS2 content for a full English playthrough.

all_releases.fidelity: Japan-only portable release with lower PSP presentation.
all_releases.reason: skip: portable route with no sourced exclusive content over the PS2 release.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced exclusive PSP content was identified; the PS2 release remains the complete primary route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced official remaster, remake, PC port, or modern console rerelease was identified.

entries.title: Way of the Samurai 3
entries.definitive_edition: Steam PC release with DLC for the main English run; Japan-only PS3 Plus for exclusive content sampling

emulation.emulator: Native Windows PC; RPCS3 or Xenia only for console-version comparison
emulation.notes: Use the native Steam release for the primary route. Use PS3 hardware or RPCS3 only if checking the Plus version's exclusive content.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native PC presentation and PC display options; PS3 Plus trades fidelity/access for exclusive content.

primary.why: The Steam PC release is the best English high-fidelity route and includes current PC conveniences and purchasable DLC, but Japan's PS3-only Plus version has exclusive extra companions/content that the PC release does not include.
primary.how_to_play: Buy Way of the Samurai 3 on Steam and install the available DLC packs if you want the most complete English PC setup. Sample the Japan-only PS3 Plus version separately for its exclusive companions and difficulty mode.

secondary.exclusive_content: Japan-only Way of the Samurai 3 Plus adds extra companions and additional content not included in the English PC release.
secondary.what_to_play: Play or sample Samurai Dou 3 Plus on PS3 only if you want that Japan-only content and can handle the language barrier.
secondary.why: This is the content-completeness exception; the PC version remains the primary for English high-fidelity play.

all_releases.fidelity: Mobile tie-in/release exists separately, not the preferred full console/PC route.
all_releases.reason: skip: not the definitive full-play route and no sourced completeness advantage over PC.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PS3 release; Japan-only Plus edition adds exclusive content.
all_releases.reason: secondary: PS3 Plus has exclusive companions/content, but PC is the better English high-fidelity primary.

all_releases.fidelity: Console port with content additions compared with the earliest PS3 release, but superseded for fidelity and access by PC.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over the PC route and no fidelity advantage.

all_releases.fidelity: Steam PC release with PC display options, achievements, cloud saves, and available DLC packs.
all_releases.reason: primary: best English high-fidelity route, with the caveat that Japan's PS3 Plus content remains separate.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PC is the best English high-fidelity route, but the Japan-only PS3 Plus version has exclusive companions/content not included in the PC version.

entries.remaster_caveats: The PC release is a port of the standard game, not the Japan-only Plus edition and not a full remaster.

entries.title: Way of the Samurai 4
entries.definitive_edition: Steam PC release with DLC for the main run; PS3 only for the removed invasion feature

emulation.emulator: Native Windows PC; RPCS3 only for PS3-version comparison
emulation.notes: Use the native Steam release for the main route. Use PS3 hardware or RPCS3 only if researching the original PS3 feature set.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native PC presentation and PC display options; PS3 has an exclusive feature but lower capture flexibility.

primary.why: The Steam PC release is the best high-fidelity route and brings the formerly PS3-only game to PC with improvements and DLC availability, but the PS3 original retains the removed player-invasion feature.
primary.how_to_play: Buy Way of the Samurai 4 on Steam and install the available DLC packs. Use the PS3 version only if you specifically want to investigate the original player-invasion feature.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original player-invasion feature removed from the PC release.
secondary.what_to_play: Use the PS3 version only to experience or document the original invasion feature, subject to any current online/service limitations.
secondary.why: PC is better for the main run, but this PS3 feature was removed from PC.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PS3 release with the player-invasion feature absent from PC.
all_releases.reason: secondary: retains an exclusive feature, but is lower-fidelity and less convenient than the PC primary.

all_releases.fidelity: Steam PC release with improved UI/gamepad/keyboard support, achievements, cloud saves, and available DLC packs.
all_releases.reason: primary: best high-fidelity main-run route, with the caveat that the PS3 invasion feature is absent.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PC is the best main-run version, but the PS3 original has the player-invasion feature that the PC port removed.

entries.remaster_caveats: The PC release is an improved port, not a full remake or remaster, and it removes the PS3 player-invasion feature.

entries.title: KATANA KAMI: A Way of the Samurai Story

emulation.notes: Use the native Steam release for capture. Console emulation is unnecessary for the primary route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native PC presentation with PC capture/display flexibility.

primary.why: The Steam PC release is the best fidelity and capture route among the simultaneous PS4, Switch, and PC releases, with the same core game and official DLC support.
primary.how_to_play: Buy KATANA KAMI: A Way of the Samurai Story on Steam and install any desired DLC. Use PS4 or Switch only for platform preference.

all_releases.fidelity: Console release at the same launch window as Switch and PC.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over the PC primary.
skip: portability option, but no sourced exclusive content or fidelity advantage over PC.

all_releases.fidelity: Steam PC release with PC display/capture flexibility and official DLC support.
all_releases.reason: primary: best fidelity and capture route with no sourced exclusive-content loss.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No platform-exclusive content split was identified across PS4, Switch, and PC.

entries.remaster_caveats: Standalone spin-off, not a remaster or remake of the main Way of the Samurai games.
